import pandas as pd

# Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the first numerical index column
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_77/training_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_77/training_1.csv"
source2_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_77/training_2.csv"

df0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)
df1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)
df2 = pd.read_csv(source2_path, index_col=0)

# Operation History:
# 1) JOIN : [["Source4_77_1", "Source4_77_2"], ["name", "school"]]
# 2) JOIN : [["Source4_77_0", "Source4_77_1"], ["school", "name"]]

# Step 1: Join Source4_77_1 and Source4_77_2 on Source4_77_1.name == Source4_77_2.school
# Rename columns to avoid confusion and ensure join keys exist

# Confirm columns:
# df1 columns: ['School ID', 'name', 'type', 'size', 'budget']
# df2 columns: ['school', 'Average Math Score', 'Average Reading Score', 'Number Passing Math', 'Number Passing Reading']

# Join on df1.name == df2.school
df1_2 = pd.merge(df1, df2, left_on='name', right_on='school', how='inner')

# Drop the redundant 'school' column from df2 after join
df1_2.drop(columns=['school'], inplace=True)

# Step 2: Join Source4_77_0 and the result of previous join on Source4_77_0.school == df1_2.name
# df0 columns: ['Student ID', 'name', 'gender', 'grade', 'school', 'reading_score', 'math_score']
# df1_2 columns: ['School ID', 'name', 'type', 'size', 'budget', 'Average Math Score', 'Average Reading Score', 'Number Passing Math', 'Number Passing Reading']

# Join on df0.school == df1_2.name
df_final = pd.merge(df0, df1_2, left_on='school', right_on='name', how='inner', suffixes=('_student', '_school'))

# Now we have all data combined, but the target schema is:
# ['School ID': int, 'name': str, 'type': str, 'size': int, 'budget': int,
#  'Average Math Score': float, 'Average Reading Score': float,
#  'Number Passing Math': int, 'Number Passing Reading': int]

# The target table is aggregated at school level, so we need to group by school attributes and aggregate student scores.

# Grouping keys (from target examples and schema):
# 'School ID', 'name', 'type', 'size', 'budget'

group_keys = ['School ID', 'name_school', 'type', 'size', 'budget']

# Aggregations:
# Average Math Score: average of math_score (from students)
# Average Reading Score: average of reading_score (from students)
# Number Passing Math: sum of Number Passing Math (from df1_2, same for all students in school, so take first or max)
# Number Passing Reading: sum of Number Passing Reading (same as above)

# But Number Passing Math and Number Passing Reading are school-level aggregates already in df1_2,
# so we can take the first value per group.

# Compute average scores from student data (df0 columns: math_score, reading_score)
agg_dict = {
    'math_score': 'mean',
    'reading_score': 'mean',
    'Number Passing Math': 'first',
    'Number Passing Reading': 'first'
}

grouped = df_final.groupby(group_keys).agg(agg_dict).reset_index()

# Rename columns to match target schema exactly
grouped.rename(columns={
    'name_school': 'name',
    'math_score': 'Average Math Score',
    'reading_score': 'Average Reading Score'
}, inplace=True)

# Ensure correct data types as per target schema
grouped = grouped.astype({
    'School ID': 'int64',
    'name': 'string',
    'type': 'string',
    'size': 'int64',
    'budget': 'int64',
    'Average Math Score': 'float64',
    'Average Reading Score': 'float64',
    'Number Passing Math': 'int64',
    'Number Passing Reading': 'int64'
})

# Reorder columns to match target schema order
target_columns = ['School ID', 'name', 'type', 'size', 'budget',
                  'Average Math Score', 'Average Reading Score',
                  'Number Passing Math', 'Number Passing Reading']

Target4_77 = grouped[target_columns]

# Write the result to the specified path
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_77/target_multisource.csv"
Target4_77.to_csv(output_path, index=False)
